results.cost_unit: decoded native function instruction bytes, not CLIF operations or whole serialized AOT

independent_audit: Downloaded GitHub artifact ZIP and matched its SHA-256 byte-for-byte with GitHub artifact digest
Inspected 35 archived files including all 12 AOT images and native disassemblies
Independently SHA-256 checked all source WATs, AOTs, disassemblies and installer receipt against manifest
Retokenized actual native instruction hex bytes from all 12 disassemblies independently and recomputed four deltas
Checked gated and ungated AOT/disassembly identity and negative-control baseline identity
Independently checked compiler binary identity list; gated binary rebuilt to exactly the earlier source-pinned SHA-256
limits: Exactly three human-authored compiler variants (not new sequence synthesis); all target compilation source unchanged other than experimental Cranelift patch
Finite value/trap executions on one x86-64 hosted runner are not a complete compiler-pass, arbitrary SSA, ABI, flags, poison/undefined, machine-state or cross-target proof
Incoming arguments semantically live after div/rem but this does not establish all physical registers always live across the transform
Matched output AOT hash equality means changed verifier policy did not change these four emitted images; it does not prove compiler correctness generally
Decoded native per-function bytes are not whole-AOT footprint, CLIF complexity or real workload runtime profitability
Old source pin from Souper merge and a later upstream main revision coexist; do not extrapolate to untested latest upstream
Draft research only. Do not merge to ZenoFCIS main or release branch or submit upstream without additional compiler-state proof and representative profitability
